name: Build a structure
summary: A builder lays out a building from a build menu, such as a headquarters, a barracks, a workshop or a forward base, inside a zone where building is allowed, and pays for it from the team's resources. The building rises over a build time while the builder works on it, faster with more builders, and the site is fragile until finished. Once standing it serves the whole team: it trains or unlocks new units, opens a tech step, or gives a forward point to buy, refit or respawn at. Enemies can shoot the site, kill the unarmed builder, and destroy or capture the finished building.
counterplay: Kill the builder: builders are weak or unarmed and are priority targets (Generals dozers and Workers, Supreme Commander engineers), so raiders who catch one stop the whole project.
Hit the site before it finishes: a build site is fragile and whatever went into it is lost when it falls (Foxhole).

Destroy or capture the building: a forward base that is knocked down or taken over can cost the builders their foothold and the stock inside it (Foxhole bunker bases change hands when the other side rebuilds the ruin).
Deny the ground: building is barred near enemy bases and in contested places (Foxhole), so holding the ground blocks expansion.
Steal the builder where the game allows it: a captured Generals dozer lets the thief build the other faction's buildings.

other_examples.unit: Construction Dozer (USA and China) and Worker (GLA)
other_examples.note: Every building of the USA and China comes from the unarmed dozer, which also repairs and clears mines; the GLA's cheap Worker builds, repairs and carries supplies. Builders are prime targets that need escorts, a dozer sent out to build a remote supply base is at risk of being stolen, and a stolen dozer builds its old side's buildings for the thief. With enough cash, a handful of Workers who escape can raise a whole new GLA base after the old one is wiped out.

sources.title: Construction dozer (Generals 1), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.note: Quotes the official description from the Generals manual.

other_examples.note: Engineers build, repair, reclaim and capture. Their tech level limits which buildings they can start, but any engineer can help finish a site once it is started, and several engineers add their build power together. They put factories and resource extractors at distant spots to claim expansions, yet cost as much as a light tank and die quickly, so they need escorts. The UEF commander's back-mounted drone helps its owner build or flies off to build, repair or capture elsewhere.

An unarmed amphibious vehicle that drives to a new spot and unpacks itself into a structure which widens the Soviet construction zone, so a smaller base can grow there. It is slow, fragile and can't pack up again once it has deployed.

shooter_analogues.unit: Construction and the Bunker Base (player-built forward base)
shooter_analogues.note: Players open a build menu, place a blueprint that turns red where it isn't allowed, and build the site by holding the tool with the materials on hand; a few players can work on one site at once, unfinished sites break easily and lose what was put in, and building is barred near region borders and enemy bases. A construction vehicle can turn part of a bunker network into a forward base where players set their respawn, and the base unlocks upgrades over time, faster the more players spawn there and keep it supplied. When it falls, the side that rebuilds the ruin owns it.

player_translation.summary: One cheap, weak builder unit (an engineer squad member, a dozer, a utility walker) opens a short build menu, places the outline of a team building in a zone its team controls, pays from the team's purse, and builds it by working on the site, with teammates helping. When it stands, the whole team gains something it did not have: new units in the buy menu, a tech step, or a forward point to buy, refit or respawn at. The building is a big, lasting target, so the match gains an objective the enemy wants to destroy.
as_user: You open the build menu with Q and see a few buildings, each with its price in team resources and what it gives the team. Pick one and a ghost outline follows your aim, green inside an allowed zone and red outside it.
Place it, then hold your build tool on the site to raise it; a progress bar fills, faster for every teammate who joins in. You can't shoot while building, so you need an escort or a quiet moment.
Your team pays, not just you: the team's purse drops as the building goes up, so the menu says who agreed (a team vote, or the commander role, decides on expensive buildings).
When it finishes, every teammate gets a message and the reward: new unit cards in the buy menu, a tech step, or a new respawn point near the front.
You repair your buildings with the same tool, and you are the one the enemy hunts, so you play carefully.
as_target: You see the outline and scaffolding from far away, with a progress bar over it and a map icon for your team once it is spotted.
Right now you can shoot the builder, who is weak and busy, or hit the site while it is fragile; anything poured into an unfinished site is lost when it falls.
A finished building is a big target: bring siege units, explosives or a saboteur to bring it down or take it over, and the reward the enemy team got from it goes away.
If you hold the ground around it, the enemy can't build there in the first place.
teammates: The builder's team escorts the builder, helps build to finish faster, and defends the new building; a turret or cover builder makes the site safer.
Everyone benefits when it finishes, which makes the building a shared goal and a reason to group up.
The enemy team sends raiders after builders and fresh sites, and siege units or saboteurs after finished buildings.
A forward base changes the front: its team respawns nearer the fight, so the enemy must push it out.
controls: Move with WASD and aim with the mouse; the builder's weak sidearm is on left mouse.
Q opens a small radial build menu (three to five buildings, with prices); pick with the mouse, then left click places the outline and right click turns it; Esc cancels.
Hold the interact key (or the build tool's fire) beside a site to build it, and on a damaged building to repair it; teammates use the same key to help.
The pattern spends one counted key (Q); the deploy-into-structure variant uses the unit's deploy key instead.
A team prompt (accept or decline) appears for buildings above a price threshold, so one player can't empty the purse alone.
feedback: Placement: a ghost outline, green in allowed zones and red outside, with the allowed zones tinted on the minimap while the menu is open.
Building: scaffolding rising, hammering sounds, a progress bar visible to both teams once seen, and a team ping when a site is started.
Finished: a team-wide banner naming the building and what it unlocked, with the new buy-menu cards highlighted.
Damage: fire and smoke on hurt buildings, a team alert when a building is under attack, and a map icon that flashes.
Destroyed or captured: a clear collapse or a flag change, and a banner telling the team what it lost.
changes_from_rts: In an RTS one commander builds the whole base and decides alone; here each player buys and plays one unit, so building spends a shared team purse, and expensive buildings need the team's agreement or a commander role.

RTS builders are cheap units that stay at the back; here the builder is a player, so building is quick (seconds, not minutes), teammates speed it up, and the builder keeps useful jobs at the front such as repairs.
Iron Harvest keeps production buildings inside the base zone; here allowed zones work the same way, with forward zones opened by captured ground or a forward base, so building follows the front line.
An RTS can have dozens of buildings; a shooter map with 48 players can't, so each team gets a short menu and caps per building type.
In an RTS a lost building is one more thing to rebuild; here what it unlocked must disappear visibly for the whole team, so destroying it feels like a goal reached for the attackers.
The RTS player reads a building's role from tooltips; here each building's job must show in its silhouette and in the team banner when it finishes or falls.

team_play.notes: A building is a team project: builders, escorts and helpers on one side, raiders, siege units and saboteurs on the other. What it unlocks belongs to the whole team, so it gives a shooter match a lasting objective that both teams fight over.

notes: Needs a team economy (a shared purse), build zones, and rules for who may spend it, all decided on the server.
Buildings are big runtime objects: navigation and collision change when one appears, and they need health, damage states, repair and capture rules.
What a building unlocks must hook into the buy menu, tech steps or respawn points, which ties this pattern to the match's economy design.
Build progress with several helpers, interruption, refunds (Iron Harvest refunds nothing once building starts) and cleanup when the match changes.
UI: build menu with prices, allowed-zone overlay, progress bars for both teams, team-wide banners and alerts.
Snowballing: a team that builds first unlocks more and wins more; building prices, build times and caps must leave room to come back.
Griefing: one player spending the team's purse on the wrong building; team approval or a commander role prevents it.
A builder who only builds may feel like he isn't playing the shooter; the builder needs a reason to be at the front too (repairs, cover, turrets).
Forward bases too close to the enemy turn into spawn-camping; allowed zones and no-build areas around objectives keep them fair.
Buildings are big and readable from above, but players must learn what each one does and why it matters to destroy it.
Allowed zones must be visible, or placement feels arbitrary.
The team must notice what a new building unlocked, or the effort feels wasted.

variants.name: Production building
variants.summary: A barracks or workshop that adds new unit types to the team's buy menu while it stands; lose it and those cards grey out until it is rebuilt.
variants.seen_in: Iron Harvest Headquarters, Barracks and Workshop, Generals and Supreme Commander factories

variants.name: Tech building
variants.summary: A building that opens the team's next tech step or a set of upgrades instead of units; it must stay standing for the step to stay open.

variants.name: Forward base
variants.summary: A small base near the front that extends the team's build zone and gives teammates a place to respawn, buy or refit; it grows more useful the more teammates use it, and the enemy can take it over.
variants.seen_in: Foxhole Bunker Base, Red Alert 3 Sputnik outpost, Supreme Commander remote factories

variants.name: Deploy into a structure
variants.summary: The unit itself unpacks into the building at a spot it drives to; it is slow and fragile on the way, and once deployed it can't move again, so choosing the spot is the whole decision.

variants.name: Builder drone
variants.summary: A small drone rides on the unit and helps it build, or flies off on command to build, repair or capture somewhere else, so the unit can fight while its drone works.

adds_strengths.why: Gives the whole team new units, a tech step or a forward base that lasts after the builder moves on.

adds_weaknesses.why: The builder is weak and busy while building, sites are fragile, and the finished building is a big target the enemy wants.

countered_by.why: Fast raiders catch unarmed builders and half-built sites away from the team (Generals dozers and Workers need escorts).
Artillery and siege units bring down finished buildings from beyond the defenders' reach.
Saboteurs and capturers take over or shut down the building (Foxhole rebuilt ruins change sides; a stolen Generals dozer builds for the thief).

open_questions: Does Shamble Frontlines want players to build bases at all, or are bases fixed by the map as in Renegade, with only forward outposts built?
Who may spend the team's purse on a building: any builder, a team vote, or a commander role?
What does a production building unlock: new unit cards for everyone, or cheaper prices for cards already in the menu?
May the enemy capture a finished building (Foxhole, capture-structure), or only destroy it?
Should a captured builder build its old side's buildings for the thief, as in Generals?

shooter_fit.reason: Gives a team shooter a lasting shared objective and a builder role (Foxhole does it at scale), but a team economy, build zones and big runtime objects are costly, and it can turn a builder into a non-shooter; best kept to a few forward buildings.
